composio.note: Composio supplies a managed Zendesk OAuth app, good for prototypes. For launch with your own branding and quota, create a custom auth config.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Zendesk app. For production you likely want your own app for your branding on the consent screen and a dedicated quota.
reasons: Managed app shows 'Composio wants to access your account' to users
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers

prerequisites.title: Zendesk account with admin rights
prerequisites.detail: A third-party app needs a Zendesk account to get a client ID, and creating OAuth clients needs admin permissions. Docs list Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise and Enterprise Plus plans.

prerequisites.title: Marketplace profile details
prerequisites.detail: Prepare short and long descriptions, regions, certification count and a company contact for Zendesk.

steps.title: Create OAuth client in Admin Center
steps.detail: Go to Apps and integrations, APIs, OAuth clients and click Add OAuth client. Enter name, client kind, redirect URLs and scopes, then save.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and have copied the secret.

steps.title: Copy the client secret immediately
steps.detail: The secret is shown fully only once; afterwards only the first nine characters are visible.
steps.done_when: Secret stored in a secure place.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Use Composio's API to create a custom Zendesk auth config with your client ID and secret. Check redirect URL is https and absolute.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Request a global OAuth client
steps.detail: For an app working with many Zendesk accounts, request a global OAuth client from Zendesk.

steps.title: Draft profile text and security answers
steps.detail: Draft the value proposition, long description and data-handling statements for review.

steps.title: Submit app and profile for review
steps.detail: Submit the app and Marketplace profile; Zendesk reviews a first-time profile together with the app.

traps.title: Review applies even if you skip the Marketplace
traps.detail: Zendesk says apps built for distribution must be reviewed whether or not they are listed in the marketplace.

traps.title: Secret is shown only once
traps.detail: Copy it at creation; later only nine characters show.

traps.title: Use the core subdomain
traps.detail: The authorization page must use the Zendesk core subdomain, not a host-mapped one.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding and shares quota
traps.detail: Users see Composio on the consent screen and quota is shared across Composio users.

blockers.symptom: Customer's app uses API tokens and stops working under new rules
blockers.what_it_means: Customers using token-based third-party apps must approve global OAuth when the developer offers it.
blockers.what_to_do: Offer global OAuth and ask customer admins to approve it.

items.reason: Quote states that OAuth requires registering the application with Zendesk.
Quote says internal-use customers are not impacted while third-party developers must meet new standards.
Quote says the changes do not apply to internal-use customers and apply to entities distributing to multiple customers.
Quote says all apps built for distribution must be submitted for review and approval, whether listed in the marketplace or otherwise.
Quote says public integrations will be required to go through Marketplace review.
Quote says an app interacting with many accounts is relevant, but says nothing about requesting a global OAuth client.
Quote states third-party developers must complete enhanced security reviews and comply with customer data handling principles.
Quote says Marketplace review ensures public integrations conform to the new standards.
Quote states app developers must conform to rules ensuring customer data is not misused or exposed.
Quote states all Zendesk Marketplace profiles are reviewed by Zendesk.
Quote says customers using API-token apps must approve global OAuth when the developer makes it available.
Quote asks for details on what the company does, services offered, and how it benefits Zendesk customers.
Quote says the profile includes a company contact Zendesk can reach to escalate to sales or support.
Quote says a first-time app or theme submission is reviewed together with the profile.
Quote says the time is hard to say exactly because it depends on pending requests and time of week.
Quotes say internal-use customers are not impacted and OAuth requires registration, but do not explicitly state that no provider review is needed; the implication is reasonable but not stated.
Quotes mention registering the OAuth client but say nothing about the Composio auth config step or the ordering of steps.
Quotes state public multi-customer apps must be submitted for review and approval and go through Marketplace review.
Quotes say review is required for apps built for distribution to multiple customers, but the quotes do not say it is always required in every case; the 'always' is a generalisation.
Quotes support review and Marketplace review, but do not establish the ordered steps (register, request global client, submit, security review) or their sequence.
Quotes say review ensures safety, security guidelines and conformance, but do not specifically say it checks identity or listing.
Quote says customers on API tokens must approve the new global OAuth method when the developer makes it available.

Quotes support that public multi-customer apps need Zendesk review and that internal OAuth needs registration, but nothing states the about-one-hour timing, no-wait claim, or that the review wait is unknown.
